decisions.reason: As software very close to our installed automation and services base and already given dedicated market visibility, it fits our strongest knowledge domain and offers good scope for rapid learning and improvement through our in-house R&D.

Although related to our software capabilities, this second archiving/reporting offer appears weakly differentiated and only lightly positioned in the market, so our absorptive capacity is better concentrated on the stronger adjacent software product and other developments.

This safety hardware builds on our existing infrastructure project know-how and was promoted as a standalone offer, suggesting enough fit and customer relevance to justify continued commercialization and incremental refinement.

The sludge extractor is closely connected to our water and process-engineering knowledge, so we are well placed to interpret early field experience and improve it within our established machinery business.

Control technology for water engineering machinery sits at the core of our accumulated automation expertise and directly supports our strategic move toward more connected and data-driven infrastructure solutions.
